1.note: Identified as Antonio de Guevara, bishop of Mondoñedo, author of the Epístolas familiares; the identification rests on the title and the description of the work.

2.note: The translator is Jerome; the work is his Latin version of the Chronicle of Eusebius of Caesarea.

3.note: Probably the Latin dictionary of Ambrogio Calepino; the identification is likely but not stated by the author.

4.note: The Greek transcription is garbled; the author explains it as meaning eternal and indestructible. Commonly read as aksios kai hikanos.

5.note: The final word is unclear in context.

6.note: The point is a guttural confusion (ḥikkiti read as hikkiti); the exact reading in the Talmud is uncertain.

7.note: The Greek word is uncertain; the Arukh reads plekton, 'woven'.

8.note: This figure is unidentified; the name is transliterated as given.

9.note: 'Book of the Great Ethics' suggests the Magna Moralia, but the reference to dreams and the word לאיברימי"או are unclear.

10.note: The Hebrew reads chapter 14 (פי"ד), which I have kept; Hilkhot Kelei ha-Mikdash has only ten chapters, so the number may be an error.

11.note: The author's etymology of me'il from 'al, 'upon'.

12.note: Aquila (with Prisca) is mentioned in Romans 16:3; the author's 'chapter 6' is kept as given.

13.note: In b. Mo'ed Katan 27a the speaker of the second statement is R. Joshua or Onkelos, depending on the reading; the author's argument implies Onkelos.
